title: Predicting Lemmas in Generalization of IC3
problem: Inductive generalization in IC3 (variable dropping) is the most time-consuming step in safety model checking. The paper proposes predicting a minimal lemma before variable dropping to potentially avoid this expensive operation.
motivation: IC3/PDR is widely used in safety verification due to its efficiency and scalability, making optimization of its bottleneck (inductive generalization) highly valuable for practical verification.
method: The approach uses counterexample to propagation (CTP) to predict a possible minimal lemma before performing variable dropping in IC3's inductive generalization phase. If prediction succeeds, the expensive variable-dropping step can be completely bypassed, directly accelerating the verification process.
key_novelty: Using CTP-based prediction to identify minimal lemmas proactively and eliminate the expensive variable-dropping phase of IC3's inductive generalization.
contributions: Novel lemma prediction approach leveraging counterexample to propagation
Method to bypass expensive variable-dropping generalization when prediction succeeds
Significant performance improvements demonstrated on comprehensive evaluation

metrics.other: success rate in lemma prediction, performance improvement

limitations: Specific failure modes and applicability limits not discussed in the abstract.
